evals.prompt: I have an existing file, quarterly_report.docx, and I need to change the title text on the cover page from "Q2 Results" to "Q3 Results". Walk me through exactly how you would make this edit, including the commands you'd run, from start to finish.
evals.expected_output: This is an edit to an existing .docx, so the correct approach is the "Edit" row of the task-routing table: "unzip → edit word/document.xml → zip (docx-js cannot open existing files)" — NOT the "Create" row ("Write a docx (npm) script"), because that row's approach is explicitly disqualified for this case by the parenthetical "docx-js cannot open existing files." Following the "Editing existing documents" section, the concrete sequence is: unpack with `unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/`; strip symlinks per `find unpacked -type l -delete`; run `python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/` so the target text is actually findable as a contiguous string; edit `word/document.xml` in place — the skill says "do NOT reformat or pretty-print"; rezip with `(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)`; and finally validate with `python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx`. The `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` command from the routing table is for the "Read" task, not for making edits, so it should not be presented as the editing method.
expectations: Agent classifies this as the routing table's "Edit an existing document" task and does not propose writing/generating quarterly_report.docx from scratch with a docx-js script.
Agent states or clearly implies the specific reason docx-js is disqualified here: "docx-js cannot open existing files."
Agent's workflow begins by unzipping the file (e.g. `unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/`) before any edit is made.
Agent edits word/document.xml directly and in place (not reformatted/pretty-printed) rather than any other file in the archive.
Agent re-zips the edited directory back into a .docx (e.g. `zip -Xr ../out.docx .`) as part of the workflow.
Agent does not present `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` as the way to make the edit (that command is for the Read task, not editing).

evals.prompt: Using docx-js, create a new single-page .docx titled "Field Report" that must be US Letter size and landscape orientation. What exact `page` settings would you put in the script, and why?
evals.expected_output: Two gotchas from the "Creating with docx-js" section apply together here. First, page size: "Page size defaults to A4. For US Letter set page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }" (DXA; 1440 = 1 inch) — so width must be set to 12240 and height to 15840, not left at the A4 default. Second, orientation: "Landscape: pass portrait dimensions and orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE — docx-js swaps width/height internally." This means the correct config keeps width: 12240, height: 15840 (the portrait Letter values) exactly as given, and separately sets orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE — it does NOT manually swap them to width: 15840, height: 12240, because docx-js already performs that swap internally; doing it by hand would double-swap and produce the wrong page shape.
expectations: Agent sets page.size.width to 12240 and page.size.height to 15840 (the DXA values SKILL.md gives for US Letter), rather than leaving the docx-js A4 default in place.
Agent does NOT manually swap width and height (e.g. does not set width: 15840 / height: 12240) to achieve the landscape look.
Agent explicitly sets orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE in the page config, alongside the unswapped portrait dimensions.
Agent explains that docx-js swaps width/height internally, which is why portrait dimensions must be passed even though the requested output is landscape.
Agent notes that A4 is the docx-js default page size and must be explicitly overridden to get US Letter.

evals.prompt: Using docx-js, build a 3-column table with column widths of 2000, 3000, and 5000 (DXA), light gray shading on the header row, followed by a bulleted list of 3 items below the table. Show me the key settings you'd use for the widths, the shading, and the list, and flag anything that could silently break rendering.
evals.expected_output: Three separate gotchas from the "Creating with docx-js" section apply. Table widths: "Tables need dual widths: set columnWidths on the table AND width on every cell, both in WidthType.DXA (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width." So columnWidths: [2000, 3000, 5000] must be set on the table, each cell in each column must also carry a matching width (2000/3000/5000 respectively), all using WidthType.DXA rather than WidthType.PERCENTAGE, and since 2000+3000+5000=10000, the table's overall width must also be 10000 DXA. Shading: "Table shading: use ShadingType.CLEAR, never SOLID (renders black)." — the header row shading must use ShadingType.CLEAR; ShadingType.SOLID would render the row black instead of light gray. List: "Lists: never insert • literally; use a numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET." — the 3-item list must be built with a numbering config using LevelFormat.BULLET, not by typing a literal "•" character into a TextRun.
expectations: Agent sets columnWidths: [2000, 3000, 5000] on the table AND sets a matching width on every individual cell in each column, not just on the table.
Agent uses WidthType.DXA (not WidthType.PERCENTAGE) for both the table's columnWidths and the per-cell widths, and notes PERCENTAGE breaks rendering in Google Docs.
Agent states or shows that the column widths sum to the table's overall width (2000+3000+5000 = 10000 DXA).
Agent uses ShadingType.CLEAR for the header row shading and explicitly avoids ShadingType.SOLID, noting SOLID renders black.
Agent implements the 3-item bulleted list via a numbering config using LevelFormat.BULLET rather than inserting a literal "•" character.

evals.prompt: I need to redline contract.docx as "Jane Smith": delete the entire paragraph "Vendor may terminate at will." and insert a new paragraph "Vendor may terminate with 30 days written notice." in its place. Walk me through the XML-level edit you'd make and how you'd confirm nothing was missed before calling it done.
evals.expected_output: Per the "Tracked changes" section, the edit and its validation both matter. Validation: "when redlining, validate with --author "<the name you redlined under>" (needs --original) — it reports any text you changed without a <w:ins>/<w:del> around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view," so the check must be run as `python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original contract.docx --author "Jane Smith"`. The insertion: "Wrap runs in <w:ins>/<w:del> with w:id, w:author, w:date attributes" — the new sentence goes inside <w:ins> with those three attributes. The deletion text element: "Inside <w:del>, the text element is <w:delText>, not <w:t>" — so the old sentence's run uses <w:delText>, never <w:t>, inside the <w:del>. Because the whole paragraph is being deleted (not just its text), SKILL.md's paragraph-mark rule applies: "A deleted paragraph mark ... means 'merge this paragraph into the next' — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a <w:del> around every run." This means both a deleted paragraph mark AND a <w:del> around every run in the paragraph are required — text markup alone is not sufficient. Finally, "The <w:del/> must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced," so within the pPr/rPr of the deleted paragraph mark, <w:del> must be placed before any sibling elements.
expectations: Agent validates the result with the --author flag set to "Jane Smith" (e.g. `validate.py out.docx --original contract.docx --author "Jane Smith"`), citing that this catches text changed without proper <w:ins>/<w:del> tracking.
Agent wraps the inserted sentence in <w:ins> and the deleted sentence in <w:del>, each carrying w:id, w:author, and w:date attributes.
Agent uses <w:delText> (not <w:t>) for the text element inside <w:del>.

Agent recognizes that deleting the whole paragraph requires both a deleted paragraph mark (signaling merge-into-next) AND a <w:del> wrapped around every run in that paragraph — not just marking the visible text as deleted.
Agent notes that <w:del/> must be ordered before the rPr's other children in the deleted paragraph mark, since the order is schema-enforced.
Agent uses "Jane Smith" consistently as the w:author value on the tracked-change elements and as the --author value in validation.

evals.prompt: I just finished a docx-js script that generates output.docx — it includes a table of contents, three sections of body text, and two embedded images. The script ran with no errors and output.docx now exists on disk. Is this task complete, or is there a required step left before I tell the user it's done?
evals.expected_output: The task is not complete. The "Verify the output" section is explicit and unconditional: "After writing a .docx, render it and look at it:" followed by the exact commands `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx`, `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page`, and `ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images`. A script exiting without errors only means the file was written; it says nothing about whether the TOC, sections, and images actually rendered correctly, which is exactly what this verification step is for. Since a multi-page document (TOC + three sections + images) is likely to produce several page images, the agent should also anticipate SKILL.md's note that "pdftoppm zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (page-01.jpg…page-12.jpg)" when looking for the generated files.
expectations: Agent explicitly states the task is NOT complete yet / flags visual verification as a required remaining step, rather than accepting a clean script run as sufficient to call it done.
Agent instructs converting output.docx to PDF via `soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf` (LibreOffice) as part of the remaining work.
Agent instructs running pdftoppm (e.g. `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page`) to produce page images.
Agent instructs actually reading/viewing the resulting page images (not merely confirming the files exist) — i.e., the "then Read the images" step.
Agent references or anticipates pdftoppm's zero-padded page-numbering behavior (e.g. page-01.jpg...page-12.jpg) when describing how to locate/list the generated images.

evals.prompt: A client emailed me contract_v2.docx and asked me to replace every instance of "ACME Corp" with "Acme Corporation, Inc." in the document body. How would you safely and correctly perform this find-and-replace?
evals.expected_output: This is an edit to an externally-received file, so the "Editing existing documents" workflow applies, with two of its steps doing specific work here. After unpacking with `unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/`, the next command is `find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted` — symlinks must be stripped precisely because this file came from a client (an external party) and is untrusted. Before attempting the replace, `python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable` must be run, because "Word splits text across many <w:r> runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML" — meaning a direct search for "ACME Corp" in the raw document.xml could easily fail to match even though the text is visibly present. Only after that should the agent edit word/document.xml in place (not reformatted/pretty-printed), rezip with `zip -Xr ../out.docx .`, and validate with `scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original contract_v2.docx` before considering the replacement done.
expectations: Agent unzips contract_v2.docx into a working directory (e.g. unpacked/) before making any edits.
Agent strips symlink entries (e.g. `find unpacked -type l -delete`) and explicitly justifies this because the docx came from an external party (the client) and is untrusted.
Agent runs merge_runs.py on the unpacked directory before attempting the find-and-replace, rather than searching the raw document.xml directly.

Agent explains the reason for merge_runs.py: Word splits visible text across many <w:r> runs, so "ACME Corp" may not exist as a contiguous string in the XML even though it's visible in the rendered document.
Agent performs the replacement inside word/document.xml, editing in place without reformatting/pretty-printing, then rezips into the final .docx.
Agent runs validate.py on the resulting file before treating the replacement as finished.
